title: Ivy leaf motif
subtitle: A three-lobed ivy leaf with a long stem, 8 cm
excerpt: The ivy leaf has a distinctive three-lobed outline — a large central lobe and two smaller side lobes — with a long stem. Worked around a centre spine chain, the ivy leaf is simpler than the oak but still immediately recognisable. At 8 cm in DK cotton it is effective as a trailing-vine applique, sewn in sequence along a blanket border.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 5 (1890), ivy and vine crochet applique chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet botanical leaf section.
heroPrompt: A crochet ivy leaf applique in mid-green DK cotton with three lobes and a long stem, 8 cm leaf body, photographed flat on natural linen in soft daylight.

chartDefinition.title: Ivy leaf motif
chartDefinition.caption: Centre spine with a stem extension. Three lobes: two small side lobes (dc/htr/dc) from the lower spine, one large central lobe (dc/htr/tr/htr/dc) at the tip.

glossaryTerms.definition: A rounded projection of a leaf outline. The ivy leaf has one large central lobe and two smaller side lobes giving the characteristic three-part ivy silhouette.

content.text: : a tall central lobe at the leaf tip and two smaller side lobes partway along. The side lobes are small chain arches worked outward from the spine and returned; the central lobe is built into the spine itself using taller stitches at the tip point. A long stem ch (4 dc along the foundation chain) extends from the base for use in trailing-vine compositions.

attrs.title: Materials for one leaf
attrs.body: About 6 g of mid-green or variegated DK cotton. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors.

content.text: Each finished ivy leaf body measures 8 cm long and 6 cm wide. The stem adds a further 4 cm. Total 12 cm tip to stem end in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
half treble (htr) — UK; US "half double crochet".
treble (tr) — UK; US "double crochet." Used at the central lobe tip.
Ch 20. Dc in 2nd ch from hook and next 3 ch (4 dc forming the stem). Sl st into the next 2 ch to anchor the leaf base.
Ch 5. Dc in 2nd ch from hook. Htr. Htr. Dc. Sl st back into the spine chain. Sl st along the spine 3 more chains toward the tip.
Dc into next 2 spine chains. Htr. Tr (central lobe tip). Htr. Dc. 3dc to turn the tip. Working back along the underside of the spine from the tip:
Dc. Htr. Dc. Sl st along spine 3 ch toward base. Right side lobe: Ch 5. Dc. Htr. Htr. Dc. Sl st back to spine. Sl st along remaining spine to the stem base. Sl st along the 4 stem dc. Fasten off.

definition.title: Ivy leaf motif
definition.caption: 20ch foundation. 4dc stem. Two side lobes (ch-5 arches). Central lobe along spine with tr tip. 3dc turn. Return with mirrored side lobe.

content.text: Weave in ends. Sew the leaf onto the base fabric. For a trailing ivy vine, sew multiple leaves in sequence, curving the stems slightly and overlapping the base of each leaf over the next stem.
Handwash with the base fabric in cool water. Lay flat to dry.
The fern frond (crochet-leaf-fern) is the more complex pinnate leaf for a contrast botanical set. The holly (crochet-leaf-holly) and oak (crochet-leaf-oak) complete a four-season leaf collection.
